data.hypothesis: With a 4096-element input tile and the unchanged 128-thread shared-memory tree, the large case produces 1024 int64 partials. Capping direct finalization at 256 adds a parallel 128-way reduction stage (to 8 partials) before the final kernel. This tests whether that stage's reduced finalizer work offsets its launch and traffic compared with the measured 4096-tile, 1024-cap two-kernel design; no speedup is assumed.

memory_lessons.applicability: Use these whole-call measurements to motivate a controlled cap comparison, not to attribute performance to any one kernel.
memory_lessons.claim: The measured 4096-tile candidate reported 7.81568 µs over three samples, while the selected 128-tile/256-cap parent reported 44.27456 µs over three samples. Since tile and finalization topology differ, their results do not isolate either cause.
memory_lessons.next_experiment: Measure the 4096-element tile with the 256-partial finalizer cap and compare repeated full-call samples to the 4096-tile result with a 1024 cap.

data.notes: The visible prior variants were valid; no failed-variant diagnostic was supplied. The 4096-tile result measured 7.81568 µs in three samples and the selected parent 44.27456 µs in three samples. These are whole-call observations, not a causal attribution. This candidate is designed as a controlled finalizer-cap comparison against the 4096-tile variant; the controller must validate and measure it.
transformations: Changed the input partial tile from 128 to 4096 elements per 128-thread CTA; each thread accumulates its strided inputs in int64 and the original shared-memory tree reduces the thread sums.
Kept the direct one-CTA input path for n <= 128 and used two packed scratch buffers for larger recursive stages without reading uninitialized scratch.
Set the finalizer cap to 256 so larger partial arrays use the unchanged 128-way shared-memory reduction before finalization writes directly to out.
Kept all intermediate sums in int64, narrowing only after the exact total is established; retained pointer and n validation and default-stream launches.
